title: The CFPB is Correcting Flaws to Restore Integrity and Utility to the Consumer Complaint System
discussion_signal: The post says CFPB complaint volume grew sharply, especially in credit reporting, and interprets new dispute sequencing, authentication, and standardized response categories as attempts to restore signal quality. It highlights a central visibility problem: more recorded complaints can mean more consumer harm, more assisted or automated submissions, or both. The discussion does not show whether affected consumers receive correction or compensation.
linked_research_question: When complaint visibility rises but submissions become more assisted or automated, what evidence still identifies genuine harm and successful consumer remedy?
limits: The post interprets CFPB changes and does not measure outcomes
Complaint volume is not a prevalence or recovery measure
The claim about sources of complaint growth requires independent validation
